root_cause.text: The `decode_choice` function in the `nf_conntrack_h323` netfilter helper uses a zero-initialized `len` variable instead of the required 2 bytes in a boundary check before calling `get_len()`, allowing an out-of-bounds read when the bitstream is fully consumed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff replaces `nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, len, 0)` with `nf_h323_error_boundary(bs, 2, 0)` in `net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_h323_asn1.c`, and the commit message explains that because `len` is 0, the boundary check evaluates to false when `bs->cur == bs->end`, causing the subsequent `get_len(bs)` call to dereference past the end of the buffer.
